messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: streaming-gateway (us-east-1) high error rate detected — 5xx spikes and chunked-decoding failures. rolling 5m error_rate=6.8% (baseline 0.3%). affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. alerts: increased client disconnects and 'incomplete chunk' logs.

sre_oncall: seeing it, joining. what started when?

maria_g: spike around 11:14 UTC, first noticed by customer X. I can pull logs.

devin_k: confirming logs show a surge of chunked decoding exceptions from the gateway dechunker: `ERROR dechunker: invalid_chunk_size: unexpected EOF` and a lot of `502 upstream reset`.

sam_ops: any recent deploys to gateway or dechunker in the last deploy window?

lisa_prod: infra-deploy bot shows a config push to gateway-proxy at 11:08 UTC (nginx: keepalive/timeout tuning + enable fast-io). Also a micro-deploy of dechunker service at 11:10 (v1.4.2).

maria_g: timeline matches. I'll tail the dechunker logs across a few hosts.

infra-pager: automated note: oncall rota = @sre_oncall (primary), fallback = @sam_ops. escalation threshold reached.

sre_oncall: quick triage — is this client cancel vs server-side chunk corruption? check streaming success rate by client user-agent.

devin_k: run: `jq -r '.req.headers["user-agent"]' access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head` — majority are our SDK v0.9.2 and some curl/okhttp. Not concentrated to a single client.

maria_g: sampling raw payloads: I see a pattern: upstream injects chunked frames, then dechunker fails to read the final CRLF for certain streams and throws. Those flows then produce `502` to client.

sam_ops: could this be related to the keepalive/fast-io change? maybe buffers getting flushed earlier. Reverting gateway config to previous commit is lowest-risk.

devin_k: agreed. mitigation plan: 1) revert gateway-proxy config pushed at 11:08, 2) temporarily set streaming fallback -> paged responses for high-error routes, 3) increase dechunker log verbosity and add telemetry to count partial-chunk errors per host.

lisa_prod: I'm applying revert to canary pool now (canary group A). will monitor.

maria_g: adding a golden rule check to prevent the specific nginx flag from landing while streaming load is high.

incident-bot: deploy started: revert gateway-proxy config (canary A) by lisa_prod at 11:25 UTC.

sre_oncall: also enable paged fallback for /v1/stream and /v1/chat/stream for 5% of traffic as a quick mitigation — can we flip a feature flag?

sam_ops: `/ops/feature-flags set streaming_fallback=on --routes /v1/stream,/v1/chat/stream --sample 0.05` — running now.

devin_k: telemetry: partial-chunk errors spiked to 420/s across 12 hosts pre-mitigation, now seeing drop in the hosts targeted by canary revert. overall 5xx rate down to 3.1%.

lisa_prod: revert rolled to 50% of hosts at 11:34, no regression on canary. continuing rollout.

maria_g: heads-up: customers on mobile SDKs reported more disconnects. paging fallback will cause higher latency for those users — flagging possible user-facing degradation.

sre_oncall: message to support: assemble CS notice template and list impacted endpoints. keep it internal first.

incident-bot: deploy succeeded: revert gateway-proxy config rolled to 100% at 11:39 UTC.

devin_k: post-revert metrics: partial-chunk errors down to 18/s, 5xx stabilized at 0.7% within 5m. looks like gateway config was the trigger. dechunker v1.4.2 amplifies the symptom under the changed pipeline but the immediate fix is the config revert.

sam_ops: still want to pin dechunker to previous stable version and run canary for v1.4.2 with added tests for chunked trailers.

lisa_prod: agreed. creating PR to roll back dechunker to v1.4.1 on non-canary clusters and schedule canary with extended validation.

maria_g: customer-impact estimate: peak window ~11:14-11:40 UTC, estimated 12k streaming sessions impacted, ~2.4k returned 5xx. initiating incident classification for postmortem.

sre_oncall: assign action items: (1) rollback dechunker on prod non-canary until fix (owner: lisa_prod), (2) add unit + integration test around chunked boundary conditions (owner: devex), (3) update runbook to include rollback steps for gateway fast-io flags (owner: sam_ops), (4) CS draft (owner: maria_g).

infra-pager: note: set SLO burn alert to watch customer-facing streaming latency for next 48h.

devin_k: quick debug snippet for postmortem: attached sample error lines:```
ERROR dechunker: invalid_chunk_size: expected 1, got -1
WARN gateway: upstream closed before final CRLF
DEBUG conn-1234: recv 0 bytes, state=half-closed
```

maria_g: I'm saving the sample payloads and anonymizing them for the postmortem.

sre_oncall: are we comfortable closing live triage? metrics look stable for 10m. I'll keep monitoring for 2h.

sam_ops: leaving the paged fallback on at 5% for the next hour, then ramp down if stable.

lisa_prod: PR #4123 created to pin dechunker -> v1.4.1 on prod and add extra chunk-probe unit tests.

incident-bot: incident timeline recorded. severity: S2 (customer impact non-critical).

maria_g: prepping customer impact note: short description, time window, mitigation steps taken, expected follow-ups (postmortem, SDK guidance).

devin_k: follow-up: we'll reproduce locally with a stress test that simulates the gateway fast-io behavior + dechunker v1.4.2 and iterate a patch.

sre_oncall: thanks everyone. postmortem owners set. I'll mark this thread as "handoff-complete" for oncall but keep it pinned for follow-ups.

sam_ops: adding an alert to detect the specific `invalid_chunk_size` error and auto-escalate next time.

maria_g: CS note drafted and reviewed, ready for internal review before external comms.

lisa_prod: rolling rollback of dechunker on non-canary clusters at 12:05 UTC.

sre_oncall: monitoring. closing live mitigation loop; leave the rest to postmortem.

incident-bot: thread auto-closed for live triage at 12:20 UTC (follow-ups remain).
